claim: The bare 弟 drops the '(My)' that its siblings 兄 and 姉 carry, so the back does not teach that the plain form is the one used for your own family, which is the contrast this chapter is built on.
evidence: 弟 back: 'Answer: Younger brother'. Same set: 兄 'Answer: (My) older brother', 姉 'Answer: (My) older sister', 弟さん 'Answer: Someone else's younger brother'.
fix: Gloss it '(My) younger brother' to match 兄 and 姉.
verdictReason: The vocabulary list glosses 弟 "younger brother" without "(my)", so the card copies the book there, but the Kinship Terms table (read from the chapter XHTML) prints 弟 in the "2. Referring to yours" cell spanning both formal and informal, with 弟さん under "Referring to other families"; the deck already ships 弟さん as "Someone else's younger brother" (r-cd29568063bd). "(My) younger brother" is what the table says and matches 兄, 姉, 父, 母 in the same unit. Polish: the card is not wrong, it just stops short of the contrast the table draws. No "(informal)" tag: the cell spans formal and informal.

claim: うちの人 is glossed without 'My', while its twin うちの子 says 'My child', so the back does not say whose husband うちの人 refers to.
evidence: うちの人 back: 'Answer: Husband (informal)'. うちの子 back: 'Answer: My child (informal)'. 主人 back: 'Answer: My husband (formal)'.
fix: Gloss it 'My husband (informal)' to match うちの子 and 主人.
verdictReason: Kinship table, Husband row: "1. Referring to other families: ご主人 | 2-A formal: 主人／夫 | 2-B informal: だんな／うちの人, etc." うちの人 is a way to refer to YOUR OWN husband, so "My husband (informal)" is the table's meaning, and it lines up with r-636e7702bc4b 主人 "My husband (formal)" and r-346413644cb8 ご主人 "Someone else's husband". Note for the fixer: r-90cc45d59ba9 嫁さん "Wife (informal)" sits in the same 2-B cell of the Wife row and has the same shape, and the Reader found 奥さん shares that cell (r-8dfa494661bc below), so the wife cards are best worded together.

claim: 別に is glossed as a stand-alone reply with no mention that it goes with a negative, so a learner who later reads 別に in a sentence has no meaning that fits; its neighbour 何も does flag the negative.
evidence: 別に back: 'Answer: Nothing in particular'. 何も back: 'Answer: Not…anything (with a negative)'.
fix: Gloss it 'Not particularly; nothing in particular (with a negative)'.
verdictReason: Book, Adverbs and Other Expressions: "なにも＋negative 何も not…anything" and "べつに＋negative 別に nothing in particular": the book marks both words with "+negative" in the same way. The deck carried the marker over for 何も (r-3f9f4a086bc1, "Not…anything (with a negative)") and dropped it for 別に, so two identical book entries got different treatment. Keep the book's gloss and add the marker: "Nothing in particular (with a negative)". Polish.

claim: The vocabulary entry 背が高い was excluded on the grounds that 高い is carded on its own, but 高い is not carded until chapter-20, so at this chapter the learner has 低い from the same split and no 高い.
evidence: Book vocabulary (い-adjectives): "せがたかい 背が高い tall (stature)" beside "せがひくい 背が低い short (stature)". Card r-f27a36c8d505 excludedReason: "Its words are carded on their own: 背, 高い." 低い (r-c022ef791faa) ships in chapter-8; 高い (r-e9d57f21b007, "Expensive; high") first ships in chapter-20.
fix: Card 高い in this unit (reading たかい, as the book prints it in 背が高い) or move the chapter-20 card here, so the exclusion reason holds.
verdictReason: Grepped every cards.json in the collection: the only 高い card is r-e9d57f21b007 "Expensive; high" in chapter-20 (Chapter 21: Reading and Writing 7), and the ledger before chapter-8 has 高 (kanji, "High", chapter-5), 高校 and 高等学校 but no 高い; たかい is not in the kana deck either. So the exclusion reason on r-f27a36c8d505 ("Its words are carded on their own: 背, 高い") is false for a learner at this chapter, while its partner 背が低い was split the same way and 低い (r-c022ef791faa) ships here. Same pattern as the 右側 finding in chapter-7. Caveat for the fixer: preflight holds one card per written form across the collection and anki-delivered.json lists r-e9d57f21b007 as delivered, so carding 高い here means moving the chapter-20 card (a scheduling-aware owner step), and its English should then cover the senses the book teaches by chapter-8 ("Tall; high; expensive").

evidence: Kinship Terms table, Wife row: "1. Referring to other families: 奥さん | 2-A formal: 家内／妻 | 2-B informal: 奥さん／嫁さん, etc." Card: 奥さん "Someone else’s wife".

verdictReason: Kinship table Wife row, read from the chapter XHTML: "1. Referring to other families: 奥さん | 2-A formal: 家内／妻 | 2-B informal: 奥さん／嫁さん, etc. | 3. Addressing yours: お母さん". 奥さん appears in both column 1 and column 2-B, so "Someone else's wife" gives half the table. claim: うちの子 is marked informal, but the book prints it in one cell spanning both the formal and informal "Referring to yours" columns.
evidence: Kinship Terms table, Child row: "お子さん | うちの子 (colspan across 2-A formal and 2-B informal) | ——". Card: うちの子 "My child (informal)".
fix: Drop "(informal)", e.g. "My child" (お子さん is already "Someone else’s child").
verdictReason: Chapter XHTML, Child row: お子さんうちの子——. The cell spans 2-A formal and 2-B informal, so the book does not mark うちの子 informal; the deck added the tag. "My child" stays distinct from r-339883a9e19c お子さん "Someone else's child". The same colspan applies to 弟 and 妹, which is why the confirmed Learner fixes for those carry "(My)" and no register tag.

claim: 七人 shows only the reading shichi-nin, though the book prints two readings for it.
evidence: Counting People table: "7 しちにん／ななにん（七人）". Card: 七人 "Seven people", ttsText しちにん, romaji "shichi-nin".
fix: Show both readings on the back (shichi-nin / nana-nin), keeping しちにん as the audio.
verdictReason: The fact is right: Counting People prints "7 しちにん／ななにん（七人）" and the back shows only "shichi-nin". But this is a deck-wide convention, not a slip on this card: six cards in the collection carry the same reviewNote "The book gives more than one reading: X, Y. Audio uses the first." (十歳 ch-16, 十分 ch-19, 毎年 ch-20, 男の人 and 女の人 ch-8, 七人), and no word card anywhere shows two romaji readings; only silent kanji cards do (七 "shichi / nana, nano"). docs/designs/reading-decks/04-card-rules.md says the romaji is made from the word's reading, singular. Fixing this card alone would leave the other five inconsistent. What settles it: an owner ruling on whether a word card's Says line may list the book's alternative readings ("shichi-nin / nana-nin") when the audio voices the first; if yes, apply to all six; if no, close as wont-fix.
